charts.title: Escalating CAC allowance into BFCM
charts.message: Don't tell your media buyer to spend more; give them an escalating CAC target on a fixed date band, spending above target CAC to build the warm audience so weekly CAC drops about 30% on BFCM and aggregate CAC comes back to target.
charts.notes: Illustrative example. Weekly CAC printed labels: $50 (Sep 24), $55 (Oct 1), $57.50 (Oct 15), $60 (Nov 5), $62.50 (Nov 12), $35 (BFCM); unlabelled weekly points (Oct 8, Oct 22, Oct 29, Nov 19) sit visually at the same level as the preceding label. Aggregate CAC labels exact only at $57.80 (Nov 19) and $50 (Sep 24, BFCM); the rest read off the chart (approx).
annotations: Pink shaded area between weekly CAC and target, Sep 24 to Nov 19: Building demand
Green shaded area between target and weekly CAC at BFCM: BFCM payback
Callout: Spend above target CAC to build the warm audience

Callout: BFCM: weekly CAC drops ~30% ($35)
Dashed gold line labelled Target CAC at $50

charts.title: The CPM ladder, from $2 to $1,000
charts.message: The ranking by CPM is almost the inverse of the ranking by attention; the cheapest way to reach 1,000 people and the best way are almost never the same thing.
charts.notes: All ranges printed as labels. Draw as floating bars [low, high] on a logarithmic x axis. Social and Super Bowl are approximate single values (~$14, ~$63) drawn as thin bars. Sources per article: Solomon Partners 2025 Major Media CPM Comparison via Adams Outdoor; McCarthy & King for direct mail.
annotations: 'Cheapest CPM' callout at Out-of-Home
'Worst CPM' callout at Direct Mail
Social (blended) printed as '~$14'; Super Bowl as '~$63' (point values)
Colours: green = Out-of-Home, Radio; blue = Social, Broadcast TV, Print, Digital; gold = Super Bowl; red = Direct Mail
stats: Billboards run a CPM of about $2 to $16. Radio, $4 to $25.
Broadcast TV runs $13 to $49. Print, $13 to $54. Digital as a whole is all over the map, $2 to $196
Direct mail runs a CPM of $500 to $1,000. Fifty cents to a dollar per piece. That is 30 to 70 times the cost of a billboard to reach the same 1,000 people.
Industry estimates put bot traffic at 10 to 30 percent of digital impressions.
it averages a 4.4 percent response rate against 0.12 percent for email
CPMs rose roughly 20 percent across 2025... conversion rates rose about 8 percent in the same window
